Without that tag the OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE does not apply and the criterion looks like an in-session evaluable check, which it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC4 checkbox to: '- [ ] [operator-attested] Both children are closed, each with its Gerrit change at `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`; verified by the change status in Gerrit before each close.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR (or AGENTS.md / design-doc section) capturing the decision to replace `_TYPE_TIER` comparability with NCA-based structural comparability, including the two rejected alternatives and the resolved-pair ancestor invariant, so the semantics are discoverable from the codebase independent of this plan.
evidence: Plan states: 'Replace type-tier comparability with structural (nearest-common-ancestor) comparability; add a resolved-pair invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of how the edge was produced'
Plan names two rejected alternatives with rationale, but this rationale lives only in the plan document, not in a persistent design artifact
No mention of ADR, AGENTS.md update, or design-doc entry anywhere in the plan

The overlay criterion flags: 'a novel architectural decision is captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design doc update' — this is a novel architectural decision (changing fundamental graph semantics) with no such artifact specified
findings.finding: The plan replaces a named policy (`_TYPE_TIER` comparability) with a novel architectural rule (nearest-common-ancestor structural comparability) that changes the semantics of blocking links system-wide, supersedes two bugs, and defines the escalation contract for all callers — but does not call for capturing this decision in an ADR, AGENTS.md, or design doc. Future maintainers encountering `resolve_hierarchy_link` will have no persistent artifact explaining why NCA was chosen over type-tier, what the rejected alternatives were, or what invariants the resolved-pair must satisfy.
scenarios: A future maintainer modifying `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` has no ADR to consult and cannot distinguish the NCA rule from an incidental implementation choice, risking re-introduction of type-tier logic or a new comparability heuristic that violates the ancestor invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Create `docs/adr/NNNN-structural-blocking-link-comparability.md` (or equivalent) that records: (1) the problem statement, (2) the NCA decision and its rationale, (3) the two rejected alternatives and why they were rejected, (4) the ancestor-blocking invariant and where it is enforced. Reference it in a comment at the top of `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py`.

findings.finding: Child 7ab3 widens escalation (cousins now escalate rather than record directly), which increases the population of silently-substituted links on the `rebar.link()` / MCP / reconciler path where `quiet=True` discards the redirect record. Neither child bounds or documents the expanded blast radius. The parent plan names the silence bug as follow-up but does not note that this change makes it more frequent.
findings.location: child 7ab3 — Approach section ('Cousins now escalate — an intended behaviour change') and Out of scope / parent plan Approach section (quiet=True note)
scenarios: An operator or agent uses `rebar.link()` or the MCP `link` tool to set a cousin dependency (task-a1 to task-b1 in different stories). Before 7ab3 this records directly; after 7ab3 it silently escalates to story-a→story-b with no observable signal to the caller. Agents wiring dependency graphs will receive no indication the requested edge was substituted.

The reconciler's inbound apply path calls `rebar.link` for every inbound dependency record; widened escalation means more records are silently rewritten on apply, with no log entry or error for the operator.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note to child 7ab3's Out-of-scope block quantifying that cousin-pair links (previously direct, now escalated) will be silently substituted on the quiet path, and reference the follow-up doctor epic by id so the expanded surface is tracked. Alternatively, add a warning log (not stdout) inside `composer.link_core` that fires when `was_redirected` is true regardless of `quiet`, so library callers have at least a log trace.

An executor must invent this contract.

Callers of `composer.link_core` and `rebar.link()` may need to handle the new rejection path differently from the existing cross-subtree escalation path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Decomposition child 1 description: 'Attempting to create an ancestor-blocking edge raises `ValueError` (or a named subclass) with a message identifying both tickets; no redirect record is emitted, since the link is structurally invalid rather than cross-subtree.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the policy for unresolvable edges during doctor repair (e.g., 'log a warning and skip; emit the skipped edge in the findings report') so the repair pass has a defined behavior for partial-failure cases.
evidence: 'the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver and cannot be written before those semantics are final'

findings.finding: The doctor repair description says 'the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver,' but does not specify what happens when an edge cannot be cleanly re-resolved — for example, if one ticket has been deleted, the hierarchy has changed since the edge was written, or re-resolution would produce a self-loop. An executor must invent the error-handling policy.
scenarios: A ticket referenced by an existing bad edge was deleted after the edge was written — re-resolution raises a KeyError or equivalent.
Re-resolution of an edge under the new rule would produce the same ancestor-blocking shape (e.g., hierarchy changed between edge creation and repair) — the repair loop could loop or error.

scenarios: A reviewer or implementer confirms AC1 and AC2 pass, misses that the guard was not relocated, and closes child 1 without the invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable 'by any path into the resolver'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'Attempting to record a blocking edge between a ticket and any of its ancestors or descendants — by any call path — raises an invariant error at the `_links.py` guard; verified by a unit test that calls `add_dependency` directly with an ancestor pair and asserts the rejection, independent of the resolver rewrite in `_hierarchy.py`.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that directly verifies `_TYPE_TIER` is no longer consulted in blocking-link comparability — e.g., a test that creates sibling tickets of deliberately mismatched types (task and story) sharing a parent and confirms a direct dependency is recorded without escalation.
evidence: 'The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the parent hierarchy alone; _TYPE_TIER no longer participates in that decision.'
No AC references _TYPE_TIER or verifies its removal from the comparability logic; the closest ACs are AC1 and AC2, which verify two specific scenarios.
findings.finding: The Success Criteria state '_TYPE_TIER no longer participates in that decision' (removal of type-tier from comparability), but no Acceptance Criterion verifies this removal — all ACs verify behavioral outputs for specific scenarios, which could pass even if `_TYPE_TIER` remains in the code path as a tiebreaker for cases not covered by AC1 or AC2.
scenarios: An implementation retains a fallback to _TYPE_TIER for ticket-type combinations not covered by the regression tests; the ACs all pass; the underlying policy defect described in the context ('comparability keyed on a ticket's type') persists for those cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'A task and a story that are direct siblings (same parent) can hold a direct blocking dependency without escalation, regardless of their types; verified by a parametrized regression test covering at least two type-mismatched sibling pairs, confirming _TYPE_TIER is not consulted.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan for the `doctor` repair pass: specify that a full store snapshot (or export of affected edges) is taken before repair begins, and describe how to restore from it if the repair must be reversed.
evidence: 'a store-wide scan plus one-shot repair for edges written under the old rule'
'The repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver'
No mention of snapshot, backup, undo command, or interrupted-repair recovery anywhere in the plan
findings.finding: The `rebar doctor` repair (child 2) performs a one-shot, store-wide rewrite of existing dependency edges. The plan acknowledges this is irreversible but provides no rollback/back-out path: no pre-repair snapshot step, no undo command, and no description of behavior if the repair is interrupted mid-pass. Per T4, acknowledgement alone is insufficient — the remedy must be an explicit rollback or back-out plan.
findings.location: Decomposition — child 2 ('`doctor` detection and repair'); Acceptance Criteria — operator-attested AC
scenarios: The new resolver has a latent bug; the repair rewrites hundreds of edges incorrectly; there is no way to restore the original edges.
The repair process is interrupted midway (process kill, disk full); the store is left in a partially-migrated state with no way to determine which edges were already rewritten.
An operator runs doctor on the wrong store; edges are permanently altered with no undo.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the repair loop runs, emit (or write to a file) the full set of edges to be modified in a reversible format (e.g., a machine-readable undo script or a pre-repair export). Document in the child 2 spec: (1) the snapshot step, (2) how to apply the undo script, and (3) that an interrupted repair is idempotent (re-running doctor on a partially-repaired store converges safely).

evidence: 'comparability is structural, and any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency' — cited as the correct rule but not argued from first principles
Rejected alternatives explain what is NOT chosen; no Approach section text explains why the NCA-sibling model is the right primitive for ready/next-batch scheduling semantics
findings.finding: The plan's Approach section states a positive rationale for WHAT to do (replace type-tier with NCA structural comparability) but does not state WHY the specific NCA-sibling model is the right structural primitive rather than, for example, a depth-equality model or a common-subtree model. The justification given is 'jira-reb-1582 asks for the rule itself to change' (an external authority), with no first-principles argument for why NCA-children-as-comparable is the correct invariant for scheduling correctness.
scenarios: An implementer who disagrees with the NCA-sibling definition (e.g., who thinks depth-equality is the right analogue) has no plan-level argument to consult and may implement a variant that passes the named test cases but violates the intended scheduling invariant for deeper hierarchies.

findings.finding: AC3 requires 'a non-empty first pass' from `rebar link-audit` run against the live repository tracker, but correctness of this outcome depends on the tracker's runtime state (whether legacy bad edges happen to exist), not on any repo artifact or fixture. If the tracker was already clean or was repaired by other means, the criterion silently fails even though the tool works correctly.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC3: '`rebar link-audit` run twice against this repository's own tracker reports a non-empty first pass…'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small synthetic store fixture with one or more edges that would have been written under the old type-tier rule. Run `rebar link-audit` against that fixture and assert: (a) first pass reports exactly those edges, (b) second pass reports none. Keep the live-tracker double-run as an informational operator step, not a required AC.

findings.finding: Context states the operator already manually unlinked the bad edge from bug 1803, but AC #3 requires the first `link-audit` pass against this repository's own tracker to be non-empty. If the manual repair also cleared every other type-tier-written edge in the tracker, AC #3's non-empty precondition could fail at verification time, making the criterion unverifiable rather than failing.
findings.location: Context section ('the operator had to retype children and hand-unlink the bad edge'); Acceptance Criteria AC #3
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase AC #3 as: 'rebar link-audit run twice produces an empty second pass after repair; if the first pass is non-empty the repair reduces it to zero, and if already empty the command exits cleanly; verified by running both passes and comparing reports.'
